title: Every Extend Extra Extreme
subtitle: An explosion starts the action instead of ending it

body: Every Extend Extra Extreme is Q Entertainment's Xbox Live Arcade action game, released on 17 October 2007. It develops an idea that began with the freeware Every Extend and continued on PSP: the player deliberately detonates a ship to trigger a chain reaction among surrounding enemies. Success depends on choosing the position and moment that allow the explosion to spread. The screen becomes more crowded as the game continues, increasing the possibilities for a larger chain. Waiting creates opportunity, but it also asks the player to remain safe until that opportunity is worth taking.

An explosion can pass from one enemy to another, growing the score as the reaction spreads across the screen. The player can halt it to collect power-ups or begin preparing the next attempt. Extra time, shields and changes to enemy speed alter what becomes possible. Losing the ship while unprotected resets the pace and multiplier, making a careless collision costly beyond the immediate mistake. The explosions also add percussion to the music, connecting the timing of a scoring decision to the soundtrack rather than treating sound as a separate accompaniment.

The Xbox 360 edition includes modes with limited or unlimited time, a more conventional shooting variation and a mode that responds to music stored on the console. High-definition visuals and surround sound extend Q Entertainment's interest in linking simple actions to a larger audiovisual response. Online competition and leaderboards give the score a shared context. The basic action remains unusually economical: the player chooses when to destroy the ship, then watches the consequences travel beyond it. Much of the challenge lies in recognising how much a single well-placed decision can set in motion.
